newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Advocates and opponents of consitutional changes will meet each other when the Commission on Elections hears a petition to hold a people's initiative to amend the Constitution. Former president Corazon Aquino and influential Catholic Bishop Cardinal Sin urge President Fidel Ramos to fight the plan to change the Charter (ALL PAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos dismisses a top Public Estates Authority official who brokered the sale of a reclaimed property to Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp (INQUIRER)
- President Fidel Ramos says there are favourable developments in the world market that can lead to a reduction in the prices of oil products (MANILA TIMES)
- The military reports that some structures in the disputed Mischief Reef in the South China Sea have been removed but says Chinese naval vessels still patrol the area (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Philippines received a total of $2.9 billion in aid pledges from donor countries during a meeting in Tokyo, the World Bank says (ALL PAPERS)

- Some 300 billion pesos worth of investments will be made by American investors in the Philippines between now and year 2001, a survey made by the American Chamber of Commerce of the Philippines shows. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Lapanday Group of Companies signs a joint venture agreement with Malaysia's NBT International Private Ltd Bhd for a $20-million banana plantation project in either Mindanao or in Sabah in Malaysia. (PHILIPINE STAR)
